text: {"claims": [{"id": "c1", "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "Read Uncommitted mode behaves like Read Committed"}, {"sid": "P1.S1", "rel": "entails", "sub": "never sees either uncommitted data"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "Read Uncommitted behaves as Read Committed, and Read Committed never sees uncommitted data; together these entail the claim."}, {"id": "c3", "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "Prior to PostgreSQL version 9.1"}, {"sid": "P4.S1", "rel": "entails", "sub": "To retain the legacy Serializable behavior"}, {"sid": "P3.S2", "rel": "entails", "sub": "except for serialization anomalies"}], "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "9.0", "op": "<", "right": "9.1"}, "reasoning": "Pre-9.1 Serializable matched Repeatable Read behavior, which excludes all listed anomalies except serialization anomalies; 9.0 is before 9.1."}, {"id": "c5", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "No sentence says Serializable is slower than Repeatable Read; monitoring overhead is noted but not an overall speed comparison, so the claim is unsupported."}, {"id": "c6", "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "doesn't always prevent errors from being raised that would not occur in true serial execution"}, {"sid": "P7.S4", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "unique constraints violations might be reported even in cases where they could not occur in a serial execution"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P7.S0 says Serializable does not always prevent non-serial errors, and P7.S4 gives an example, contradicting “can never.”"}, {"id": "c9", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "No passage compares Repeatable Read and Serializable speed across workloads; the noted overhead for Serializable does not establish the universal claim."}]}
